ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the input terminal, a two-wire transmission line marked Γ and Z0 = 50Ω. This input line first passes through a 50Ω transmission line section marked λ/4 to reach the tapping point on the right. After the tapping point there are two parallel branch transmission lines, each also marked Z0 = 50Ω and with length λ/4; the end of the upper branch is connected to a 100Ω resistor, and the end of the lower branch is connected to a 200Ω resistor. Reasoning: For a lossless λ/4 transmission line, the input impedance transformation is Zin = Z0^2 / ZL. The upper 100Ω load is transformed through its λ/4 branch to the tapping point as 50^2 / 100 = 25Ω. The lower 200Ω load is transformed through its λ/4 branch to the tapping point as 50^2 / 200 = 12.5Ω. The two branches are in parallel at the tapping point, so the equivalent impedance is 25 || 12.5 = (25 × 12.5)/(25 + 12.5) = 25/3Ω. This tapping-point load is then transformed through the input-end λ/4, 50Ω line section, and the input impedance is Zin = 50^2 / (25/3) = 300Ω. Relative to the 50Ω input line, the voltage reflection coefficient Γ = (Zin - Z0)/(Zin + Z0) = (300 - 50)/(300 + 50) = 250/350 = 5/7.

raw_record.question_text: The parallel branches of a 2-wire transmission line are terminated in \(100 \, \Omega\) and \(200 \, \Omega\) resistors as shown in the figure. method.method_draft: First describe the diagram as a λ/4 main 50 Ω line feeding two parallel λ/4 branch lines, also 50 Ω, terminated by 100 Ω and 200 Ω. Transform each load through its branch: 100 Ω becomes 50^2/100 = 25 Ω and 200 Ω becomes 50^2/200 = 12.5 Ω at the junction. Combine these two transformed branch impedances in parallel to get 25 || 12.5 = 25/3 Ω. Then transform this junction load through the input λ/4 section: Z_in = 50^2/(25/3) = 300 Ω. Finally compute the voltage reflection coefficient at the 50 Ω input line: Gamma = (300 - 50)/(300 + 50) = 5/7.
